title: Low-cost microtome fixture for real trials
summary: A bench fixture that replaces the costly rotary microtome in a real trial. It is built from the task's own modelled parts, at full size and in the same positions: a plywood housing; a printed handwheel whose handle pin locks only at 12 o'clock; a printed specimen head on two 8 mm rods, driven through its 59 mm stroke by a crank pin in a yoke slot; a sprung cassette clamp with its lever (longer and lower than the instrument's, as in the simulation, so a gripper fits behind it); and a knife holder with a dull mock blade and a hinged guard with stops. The robot meets the same shapes, positions, strokes and operating forces as in the simulation. Only the housing's outside differs from a real instrument, and the robot never handles it. A real Leica RM2125 RTS can be used instead where one is available: the scene follows it.

features.name: Clamp spring mount
features.value: LC 030D 12 S: OD 7.62, ID 6.10, free 38.10, solid 10.52 mm. Spring axis x 466, y 49. Rocker pivot y 10, z 201.45 at start; rocker top at z 203.45. Follower seat z 207.45 at rest; bridge underside z 243.10. Installed spring length 35.65 mm, preload compression 2.45 mm. A separate 80 x 5 mm smooth guide rod passes through 5.2 mm bridge bore; spring around rod. Polish rod/bore, wax tip.
features.tolerance: seat spacing +-0.2 mm after shimming; guide bore 5.2-5.3 mm
features.check: measure 35.65 mm seat spacing at rest. At 15 degrees spring length about25.1 mm; at25.78 degrees about16.6 mm, always over10.52 mm solid height. Pull follower without spring: guide drag below0.1 N. Force acceptance3.5-5.5 N at foot at15 degrees; shim upper spring seat only within documented preload range2.1-3.1 mm, then recheck travel.

forces.name: Handwheel turning
forces.model: 0.6 N m Coulomb friction on the wheel (7.1 N at the 85 mm knob)
forces.set: neoprene washer (BOM 2) between the inner bearing and the 5/8 in clamp collar (BOM 4), with a disc spring (BOM 3) behind the collar; slide the collar along to set the squeeze and tighten its screw
forces.check: spring scale (BOM 14) hooked on the knob, pulled square to the arm: 6 to 9 N while it turns

forces.name: Handle push-in
forces.model: 4 N Coulomb friction on the handle's 10 mm slide
forces.set: an 8 mm nitrile O-ring (BOM 10) on the pin, seated in a 10.5 mm, 2 mm deep counterbore on the wheel's inner face, so the pin drags through it
forces.check: spring scale (BOM 14) on the knob end, pushed along the axle: 3 to 6 N while it slides; the lock pin drops in only with the wheel at 12 o'clock

forces.name: Clamp lever
forces.model: rocker spring 1.2 N m/rad with 0.07 N m at rest; the lever's foot 101 mm below the pivot
forces.target: 3.5 to 5.5 N at lever foot, 15 degrees open; calculated nominal 4.35 N, lip about10 mm up. Spring remains clear of solid height through0.45 rad model stop.
forces.set: Lee Spring LC 030D 12 S (0.753 N/mm;38.10 mm free;10.52 mm solid), vertical around5 mm guide rod, between bridge underside and printed follower. Rest length35.65 mm gives2.45 mm compression and0.072 N m at39 mm moment arm. Follower tip slides on rocker top at fixed y49,39 mm ahead of pivot; raised bridge underside z243.10. A separate guide rod keeps spring axial; no spring-end side bending. See spring-calculation.md for geometry/tolerances.
forces.check: Before each session: measure rest seat spacing35.65 mm, verify follower slides with under0.1 N drag without spring, then spring scale on foot pushed +y:3.5-5.5 N at15 degrees. Set lever temporarily to0.45 rad with protractor and check at least3.48 mm spring clearance above solid (length>=14.0 mm). Do not use coil bind as stop. This is a build acceptance procedure, not a claim of physical measurements already made.

forces.name: Head held by the wheel
forces.model: carriage driven only through the crank; the wheel's friction holds it
forces.target: the head stays where the wheel leaves it
forces.check: with the handle out and let go at 3 o'clock, the head does not drift down

forces.name: Knife guard
forces.model: free hinge (damping only) with stops at 0 and 190 degrees
forces.target: rests on either stop by its own weight
forces.set: free on its two shoulder screws
forces.check: folded over, it stays over the edge; folded down, it stays forward

notes: Safety: the fixture has no cutting edge. The mock blade is dull shim stock, so a gripper that reaches between clamp and knife is still scored 0 for good, as in the simulation, but is not hurt.
Housing outside: the plywood walls stand where the instrument's covers are, so the robot's clearances are the same; the robot never handles the housing.

Prices were read from the sellers' pages or search listings on 2026-11-18, before shipping and tax; they move, so treat the total as an estimate. For comparison, a used Leica RM2125 lists at about 2,100 USD and a refurbished one at about 3,400 USD (search listings, 2026-11-18).
Tools assumed: an FDM printer with a 220 x 220 mm bed (PLA, 3 perimeters, 15 to 20 % infill), a saw for the plywood, a drill with 4.2, 5.2, 8, 13 and 16 mm bits, an M4 tap and a file.

Positions are the task's assembly coordinates: millimetres from the midpoint between the arm bases, x forward, y left, z up from the bench top; the instrument stands 80 mm further out than the instrument's own layout numbers in task.py (task.XS).

Revision of spring/mount and cassette-height documentation: manufacturer data and complete travel/force calculations are in spring-calculation.md. Spring price checked2026-11-22; guide rod5 USD is an explicit budget allowance. No physical force measurement is claimed. Task simulation, instruction, scorer and demo are unchanged; existing evaluation media are retained.

cheapest.outro: With the printed cassette there is no consumable to buy: the floor is the hardware, about 129 USD, and about 96 USD for a lab that already owns a printer, filament, screws, glue and a spring scale. A lab that wants the real moulded cassettes adds BOM 12-13 (about 82 USD for a box of 500 and wax).
